sc: Lethargic, cannot drink, skin pinch 3 seconds → Severe dehydration: Plan C
Restless, irritable, drinks eagerly, slow skin pinch → Some dehydration: Plan B (ORS 75 ml/kg in 4 h)
Bilateral pitting oedema, flaky-paint skin, sparse pale hair, apathy → SAM with oedema
f: General condition · eyes · drinking · skin pinch · two signs in the same row decide the class
Ringer lactate 100 ml/kg: infant 30 ml/kg in 1 h + 70 in 5 h · improving: urine, stronger pulse → ORS
MUAC, weight-for-height, bilateral oedema (3 s thumb pressure) · appetite test · complications
With oedema: flaky skin, flag sign, apathy, big liver · without oedema: old-man face, baggy pants · stunting: low height-for-age
ReSoMal 5 ml/kg every 30 min (no ORS, no Plan C) · shock: IV 15 ml/kg over 1 h · overload: stop
Puffy eyelids = overhydration · faster breathing + bigger liver in SAM = fluid overload
trap: Standard ORS and Plan C are not used in SAM · a wasted child with slow skin pinch but no diarrhoea has wasting, not dehydration · weak distended abdomen after diarrhoea = hypokalaemia
